messages:
Raj: FYI seeing a spike of Pending GPU pods in us-west-2-gpu this morning, lots of small workloads blocking a few large inference replicas. errors look like FailedScheduling: 0/40 nodes are available: 18 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 22 node(s) didn't match Pod's node selector.

infra-bot: [alert] 2024-09-14T08:06:21Z cluster-autoscaler: scaleUp: triggered for nodegroup=usw2-gpu-pool (want 3 -> 6) — provisioning in progress :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Raj: Autoscaler kicked but new nodes are coming up as 1x GPUs with mixed MIG profiles. The large replicas need contiguous 1xA100 (no MIG) — they never fit on the new nodes because MIG slices are populated by small jobs.

Alice: Can you paste the kubectl describe + failed scheduling event?

Raj: pasted: 
`Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m    default-scheduler  0/40 nodes are available: 18 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 22 node(s) didn't match Pod's node selector`

Maria: This is classic fragmentation from mixed MIG profiles + autoscaler creating only shared-gpu nodes. Small pods request 1/4 GPU in our admission webhook as `nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb` and end up occupying slices spread across nodes. Large ones request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and still need a whole physical GPU (or a node with compatible big-profile MIG).

Jon: Right — cluster-autoscaler treats nvidia.com/gpu as scalar, but it doesn't reason about MIG topology. CA sees "fits on node" because allocatable numbers look okay, but scheduler fails due to profile mismatch.

Alice: Short term: can we patch the scheduler binding or add a nodeAffinity to prefer nodes labeled `gpu-profile=full` for big replicas? Also create a dedicated nodepool with non-MIG GPUs for the big jobs.

Raj: Proposed quick fixes:
- spin up a new nodepool `usw2-gpu-full` (size: p4d/8g, no MIG config)
- add `nodeSelector: gpu-profile=full` to large workload k8s manifests
- update CA autoscaling config to include the new pool and set `maxNodeProvisionTime` to 15m

ops-sre: We should also adjust CA expander to `least-waste` so it prefers nodes that minimize leftover fractional GPUs for small jobs. That reduces churn.

Maria: Long-term: our admission webhook should annotate pods with MIG profile intent. Then we can use an admission controller + taints/tolerations to pack similar profiles onto the same nodes. Also consider a scheduler plugin or using Karpenter which has more flexible provisioning per-slice.

Jon: For immediate triage I ran a Karst query and found 120 small GPU pods distributed across 60 nodes (2 per node), leaving 40 nodes with partially used GPUs. Packing them would free ~24 full GPUs.

Raj: Command I ran: 
`kubectl get pods -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,CPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.cpu,GPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.nvidia.com/gpu | grep gpu`

Alice: If we can't drain those nodes safely (stateful inference), we should add a disruptive schedule: cordon a few shared nodes, evict low-priority test jobs, and let CA scale new full-GPU nodes, then migrate big replicas. Needs maintenance window.

ops-sre: Agreed. Also bump PodPriority for production inference so preemption can reclaim fragmented slices from low-priority jobs.

Raj: Quick cost note: adding full GPU nodes upfront raises committed spend, but the freed placement means fewer forced retries and lower tail latency. estimated delta ~ +$6k/month vs swapping 20x small preemptible slices during peak which costs ~+$12k in retries and latency penalties.

infra-bot: deployment: created ticket INF-4821 in infra board — https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-4821 — `Create full-gpu nodepool + admission annotations`

Maria: Action items:
- Jon: create `usw2-gpu-full` nodepool template and test with a canary large replica (ETA 4h)
- Alice: add `gpu-profile=full` nodeSelector to prod inference manifests and submit PR (ETA 2h)
- Raj: coordinate maintenance window and run cordon/evict plan for 6 nodes (ETA today afternoon)
- ops-sre: update CA expander and set preemption/priorities (ETA EOD)

Jon: Will also add a CA scale-up delay guard so we don't create too many tiny shared nodes in response to small cascades.

Alice: Leaving a note: when we create `usw2-gpu-full` ensure KMS keys for nodepool match private deployment policies (security asked yesterday).

Raj: Thanks — ping me in thread when the canary is up. :thumbsup:

ops-sre: I'll monitor scheduling events and post a summary after the maintenance window.

infra-bot: [info] 2024-09-14T12:10:02Z ticket INF-4821 assigned to Jon, Alice, ops-sre

Jon: Can confirm canary large replica started on the new pool — logs show no FailedScheduling after node came online. Dropping some telemetry to check tail latency.

Maria: Great — if metrics look good we should roll this across prod regions and add an RFC for changing how we surface MIG intent to the scheduler. :rocket:
